In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incidence of low weight babies is high and that it is associated with a variety of factors.
low birth weight babies are born to mothers who are young and primiparous, with significant antenatal and perinatal problems and with poor socioeconomic background.
low birth weight babies are the outcome of the interplay of multiple risk factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
low birth weight babies are more often seen in mothers belonging to the age groups of 19-30 years, primiparous and with significant obstetric complications.

low birth weight babies are more likely to be small for gestational babies than preterm neonates and that mothers in the age group of below 19 years and above 25 years are at a high risk of delivering low birth weight babies.
the incidence of LBW babies is high enough in our country to warrant a national programme for the control of LBW.
The main takeaway from our work is that
primiparous mothers in the age group of <25 years are at a high risk of delivering a low birth weight baby.
primiparity is a risk factor for the occurrence of low birth weight and that the age group of the mothers is an important risk factor for the same.
